variables.reason: The ledger defines Ra as the first-order absolute moment (arithmetic mean roughness) of surface height fluctuations. KB record pq_arithmetic_mean_roughness explicitly names this quantity (arithmetic mean roughness, symbols Ra, R_a) and defines it as the mean absolute deviation of surface height with si_unit m and si_dimension L. That KB canonical definition is the same physical quantity used in the problem (surface roughness height statistic), so its length dimension (L exponent = 1, all others zero) justifies confirming the candidate vector. The cited record applies because it matches the ledger variable name, symbol, and the exact physical definition used in the problem context (surface-height statistic).

The ledger defines kt as the peak-to-valley height (vertical height difference between highest and lowest surface points). KB record pq_peak_to_valley_height is the canonical entry for mean peak-to-valley roughness height (symbols include kt) and specifies si_unit m and si_dimension L. The record matches the ledger symbol and physical definition (a height difference), so the length-only exponent vector is correct for kt in the original problem.

The ledger defines k_rms as the root-mean-square height of surface fluctuations. KB record pq_rms_roughness_height defines root-mean-square roughness height (symbol k_rms) with si_unit m and si_dimension L. The canonical KB definition corresponds directly to the ledger variable (RMS height about the mean), therefore the pure length exponent vector is appropriate and confirmed.

The ledger defines Sk as skewness of roughness height fluctuations (third standardized moment). KB record pq_height_skewness names surface-height skewness (symbols Sk) and defines it as the third standardized moment with si_dimension 1 (dimensionless). The KB entry matches the ledger variable name, symbol, and statistical-moment definition used in the problem, so the zero exponent vector is justified.

The ledger defines Ku as kurtosis of roughness height fluctuations (fourth standardized moment). KB record pq_height_kurtosis defines surface-height kurtosis (symbols Ku) as the fourth standardized moment with si_dimension 1 (dimensionless). The KB canonical definition corresponds to the ledger variable and confirms all SI exponents are zero.

The ledger defines ES as effective streamwise slope (mean slope in flow direction). KB record pq_effective_surface_slope defines effective surface slope (symbols ES) as the mean absolute gradient of surface height in a horizontal direction and explicitly notes a surface-height derivative is length divided by length and is dimensionless (si_dimension 1). The KB entry matches the ledger physical definition, so all SI exponents zero is correct.

The ledger defines Po as surface porosity (fractional area of voids). KB record pq_porosity defines porosity (symbols Po) as a fraction of void or open volume/area with si_dimension 1 and explicitly notes it is a dimensionless fraction. The KB entry matches the ledger variable's name and definition, so the zero exponent vector is correct for Po.
